LESSON OBJECTIVE
Identify and interpret positive association in scatterplots, tables, and real-world contexts; use positive-slope trend lines to predict.
CORE IDEA
Positive association means that as one variable increases, the other tends to increase. The points generally rise from left to right.
KEY DEFINITIONS

Scatterplot: points showing paired numerical data. Association: a pattern between variables. Line of best fit: a line approximating a trend. Correlation r: a number from −1 to +1 describing linear direction and strength.
CORE RULE
An upward pattern has positive association. A positive-slope line has m>0. For a linear trend, +r indicates positive direction, and r near +1 indicates a strong positive pattern.
HOW IT WORKS
1. Read x and y labels. 2. Scan points from left to right. 3. Check whether y generally rises. 4. Assess scatter and outliers. 5. Use a best-fit line for approximate predictions.
WORKED EXAMPLE 1 — EXACT PATTERN
Points (1,3),(2,5),(3,7),(4,9),(5,11) follow y=2x+1. The positive slope 2 gives a perfect increasing pattern.
WORKED EXAMPLE 2 — NOISY TREND
Paired values (1,2),(2,5),(3,4),(4,8) still show an overall upward tendency, even though y does not increase at every single step.
WORKED EXAMPLE 3 — LINE OF FIT
A line through (2,5) and (6,13) has slope (13−5)/(6−2)=2. A positive slope confirms upward association; the model rises by 2 y-units per x-unit.
WORKED EXAMPLE 4 — PREDICTION
If the trend line is y=2x+3, at x=7 it predicts y=2(7)+3=17. A prediction is approximate when the data are scattered.
WORKED EXAMPLE 5 — RESIDUAL
If a model predicts 14 but an observation is 16, the residual is observed−predicted=16−14=2. Residuals measure deviation from the trend line.
VERIFIED SCATTERPLOT
The five plotted points (1,3),(2,5),(3,7),(4,9),(5,11) satisfy y=2x+1 exactly. The upward line is deterministic and checked by substitution.
COMMON MISTAKES
Positive association does not require every pair to rise. A single outlier can distort the pattern. Positive association does not prove that one variable causes the other.
EXAM STRATEGY
Check the overall direction before estimating strength. Read a line's slope for rate of change; calculate residual as observed minus predicted. Avoid extrapolating far beyond the data.
QUICK CHECK
If r=+0.83, the linear association is strong and positive. If a trend line has slope −2, the association is negative. For y=3x+1, a 2-unit x increase predicts a 6-unit y increase.
LESSON RECAP
Upward trend = positive association. Positive slope and positive r support that conclusion. Association is not causation.
